In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms underlying the neurotoxicity of the inflammatory cytokine, interleukin- 1 (IL- 1).
the role of astrocytes in neurotoxicity associated with inflammation.
the mechanisms by which inflammatory cytokines induce cell death in the central nervous system (CNS).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

IL-1-induced neuronal cell death is mediated by MMP-9 released by IL-1-activated astrocytes and by uPA expressed on neuronal membranes, and that these proteases may contribute to neuronal death in CNS diseases.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MMP-9 and uPA are involved in IL-1-induced neuronal death.
MMP-9 and uPA are involved in the pathogenesis of IL-1 neuroinflammation.
IL-1beta induces neurotoxic effects in glial-neurone coculture through an MMP-9 and uPA-dependent mechanism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MMP-9 is released from astrocytes in response to IL-1, and MMP-9 is responsible for IL-1 neurodegeneration.
MMPs mediating neurotoxicity are induced by IL-1 and not by the primary insult.
IL-1-induced astrocytic MMP release is a novel mechanism of neuronal death that may contribute to neuronal death in neuroinflammatory diseases such as stroke and multiple sclerosis.
